summary:
Bullpen_fatigue and hitting are the two categories carrying this slate, and the numbers are getting hard to ignore. Across R1-R4, bullpen_fatigue has flipped from a sub-.500 season number (46-47%) to 16-8 (67%) over the last 14 days, a +20 to +21 point swing in every single rating. Hitting is even louder — R4's hitting cell is 19-5 (79%) over 14 days, a +27.0pt jump off a 52% baseline, and R2/R3 aren't far behind at 71% with +21+ pt deltas. Bullpen is the third hot category across the board, sitting at 15-9 (62%) for all four ratings with R1/R2/R3 all riding 4-game bullpen streaks. The one category to fade right now is trends — every rating shows a 3-game losing streak there at 54% over the last 14, well off the 56-58% season marks. If today's board has a trends-only pick with no hitting or bullpen_fatigue confirmation, treat it with caution; if hitting and bullpen_fatigue line up together on the same side, that's your greenlight.

Strong-play units back this up cleanly: R1 is 6-2 (+6.0u) over 14 days and 49-24 (+33.0u) over 30, R2 and R3 are both 4-1 (+6.0u and +4.0u) in the same window, while R4 has cooled to 1-2 at 7 days despite a strong 30-day base (44-24, +35.0u) — worth trusting R4 strong plays less aggressively today until it resets. On team trends, lean into LAD and TBR if either appears on tonight's card — LAD strong plays are 28-7 (80%, +27.0u) and TBR 26-10 (72%, +22.0u), both best-in-class when liked. Avoid leaning on NYY even if the model flags it; strong plays there are 9-14 (39%, -4.0u), the only team in the sample bleeding units. Category-combo-wise, trends+sp (57.8%, n=630) and trends+runs (57.0%, n=695) remain the highest-probability agreement pairs for tie-breaking close boards, but given trends' current 3-game skid, weight today's hitting/bullpen_fatigue overlap higher than usual when the combos disagree.
